	// re-posed from the live controller every frame, per eye, at zero latency (RenderHUDModel, models.cpp:226
	// -> VRMode::GetWeaponTransform -> hw_openxrdevice.cpp:431-459); the beam was UBQS_BeamGlow, a world
	// actor moved once per 35 Hz tic and interpolated between. Two layers drawn at two different moments
	// cannot agree, and no overlap slider was ever going to make them. So the hilt is placed HERE, in the
	// same tic, from the same predicted pose as its beam.
	// WHY ONLY ONE CALL: GlowPredict keeps a rolling three-sample history (gT0..gT2 / gB0..gB2 / gD0..gD2)
	// plus one hysteresis bit. Call it twice in a tic -- once for the hilt and once for the emitter, which is
	// what the obvious version of this change does -- and the second call pushes the FIRST call's
	// extrapolation in as a fresh sample, so the velocity it measures and the lead it applies both COMPOUND
	// and the saber runs away on fast swings. So it is called once, on the HAND, the one thing the hilt and
	// the beam both hang off; the emitter is rigid on it and BladeGlow derives it from this answer.
	// IT IS SAFE TO FEED IT THE FRAME'S OWN BLADE DIRECTION: of the 31 md3 frames the states only ever ask
	// for 0, 1, 2, 13-18 and the twirl, and UBQS_Data.Yaw() is 0 and Up() is 50 on every one of those nine --
	// so across every frame this history can span, BladeDir() is a pure function of the controller pose and
	// there is no frame step for the predictor to mistake for a swing. (The twirl is the one place the frame
	// really does move the blade, by 36 degrees a step, and it is forgotten rather than predicted; see below.)
	private void PoseTick()
	{
		// NOT IN THE HAND -- thrown, merged into the staff, or simply not the ready weapon. Nothing to draw,
		// and the history is stale: a saber caught or re-selected must appear where it IS, not slide in from
		// wherever it last was.
		if (!owner || thrown || merged || !InHand())
		{
			PoseForget();
			return;
		}
		lastSizeIdx = SizeIdx();            // the ui telemetry reads it, so set it even with the beam off
		if (snapQuiet > 0) gN = 0;          // a snap turn / teleport is not a swing
		// THE TWIRL STAYS IN THE HAND LAYER (and A_UBShow leaves it alone to match). A twirling staff has its
		// beam OFF -- DoEffect takes the TwirlDisc branch and calls BladeGlowOff -- so there is no
		// hilt-to-beam seam there to fix, and the twirl's V blocks carry the whole double blade as solid
		// geometry, which in the world would be sliced by every wall it swept through. Nothing to gain,
		// something to lose. The history is forgotten ACROSS it, because the twirl's 36 degrees a step is
		// baked into md3 frames 21..30 by the generator: a history spanning the boundary would read a
		// 50-degree frame change as a 1700 deg/s swing and fling the whole saber out to its 35-degree cap.
		// Forgotten, the first tic after a twirl simply places itself where it is, with no slide.
		if (UBQS_Data.IsTwirl(frameNow))
		{
			PoseForget();
			return;
		}
		gJump = !GlowPredict(HandPos() - owner.pos, BladeDir());
		if (!WorldUp())
		{
			// the psprite draws the saber this tic -- but the BEAM still gets its one prediction above, so
			// ubqs_world_saber 0 is exactly the beam the owner has today.
			if (wsaber) { wsaber.Destroy(); wsaber = null; }
			return;
		}
		// THE HILT'S OWN FRAME at the hand's unpredicted pose, in METRIC space: unit vectors built from the
		// three angles, which is exactly what the world renderer's own rotations make before
		// CorrectPixelStretch squashes world Z. md3 +X is the blade axis (BladeDirOf's own fw, and
		// UBQS_Thrown.BladeVec) and md3 +Z is the blade plane's up (UBQS_Data.GlowAxis, which IS the
		// renderer's +Z for an actor at these three angles -- checked numerically against its matrices).
		// NOTE: no UBQS_Data.TwAngle here, ever. The twirl never reaches this line, and adding it to the
		// actor's roll as well as to the vertices would turn the staff twice.
		double wa = HA(), wp = HP(), wr = HR();
		Vector3 fw = (cos(wp) * cos(wa), cos(wp) * sin(wa), -sin(wp));
		Vector3 uz = UBQS_Data.GlowAxis(wa, wp, wr);
		// ... led by the SAME turn GlowPredict gave the beam's axis, which is what makes the two one body
		if (gPAng != 0.0)
		{
			fw = GlowRot(fw, gPAx, gPAng).Unit();
			uz = GlowRot(uz, gPAx, gPAng).Unit();
		}
		// THE ORIGIN'S NUDGE IS TAKEN HERE, BEFORE THE DRAW/HOLSTER ROTATION. In the HUD chain the engine's
		// (0, 5, 30) and the MODELDEF Offset sit OUTSIDE that rotation (models.cpp:230 and :251 against :263)
		// and the pivot is zero (Weapon.BobPivot3D defaults to (0,0,0) and this saber does not set it), so
		// raising or lowering the saber turns the model's AXES and does not move its ORIGIN at all.
		Vector3 at = owner.pos + gPRel + UBQS_Data.WorldNudge(fw, uz, bOffhandWeapon, SizeIdx(), level.pixelstretch);
		// ... then the draw / holster rotation, in the model's own forward-up plane (= about its md3 +Y, see
		// PspY). Done here rather than as a MODELDEF PitchOffset because a MODELDEF key cannot be animated.
		double rho = -(PspY() - 32.0) / 4.0;
		if (rho != 0.0)
		{
			Vector3 f2 = fw * cos(rho) + uz * sin(rho);
			uz = uz * cos(rho) - fw * sin(rho);
			fw = f2;
		}
		// ... and back out the actor's three angles from that frame: the exact inverse of GlowAxis, the same
		// kind of solve UBQS_BeamGlow.Place does from its own. With no lead and no raise/lower rotation this
		// returns exactly (HA(), HP(), HR()), which is the recipe both matrix chains solve to.
		double pa = VectorAngle(fw.x, fw.y);
		double pp = -asin(clamp(fw.z, -1.0, 1.0));
		Vector3 u0 = (sin(pp) * cos(pa), sin(pp) * sin(pa), cos(pp));
		Vector3 l0 = (-sin(pa), cos(pa), 0);
		double pr = atan2(-(uz dot l0), uz dot u0);
		// the same (sprite, frame) pair A_UBShow would have drawn -- SpriteNow() for the size, the colour and
		// one blade or two, frameNow for the animation. MODELDEF is keyed on (class, sprite, frame)
		// (models.cpp:1313) and the world draw reads actor->sprite / actor->frame straight
		// (hw_sprites.cpp:885), so this is how every one of those is chosen, per tic, from ZScript.
		int spr = GetSpriteIndex(SpriteNow());
		bool hj = gJump;
		bool mir = UBQS_Data.WorldMirror(bOffhandWeapon);
		if (wsaber && wsMirror != mir)
		{
			// he changed hands mid-level (vr_control_scheme is CVAR_ARCHIVE|CVAR_GLOBALCONFIG, so he can):
			// the class carries the parity, so the other one has to be built. One tic with no hilt.
			wsaber.Destroy();
			wsaber = null;
		}
		if (!wsaber)
		{
			// THE HANDEDNESS IS THE CLASS. See UBQS_Data.WorldMirror: the engine reflects whichever hand has
			// physical index 0, which is the OFF hand under the default right-handed vr_control_scheme and
			// the MAIN hand under a left-handed one. A world actor is never reflected, so the parity goes
			// back into the MODELDEF yscale sign -- which means two classes, and this is where one is picked.
			wsMirror = mir;
			wsaber = UBQS_WorldSaber(Actor.Spawn(mir ? "UBQS_WorldSaberOff" : "UBQS_WorldSaber", at));
			if (!wsaber) return;
			hj = true;
		}
		wsaber.Place(at, pa, pp, pr, UBQS_Data.WorldScale(SizeIdx()), spr, frameNow, hj, gSnapA, gSnapL);
	}
	private void BladeGlow(Vector3 base, Vector3 dir, double len, Vector3 pom)
	{
		double str = UF("ubqs_blade_glow", 0.6);
		// retracted (or off): no glow at all -- it comes back fresh, so nothing sweeps in from where it was
		// A LOCK BRINGS THIS ONE UP whatever ubqs_blade_glow says, because it is the half of the swap
		// that looks right when the blades are crossed. 0.6 is its designed strength.
		if (Locked() && str <= 0.01) str = 0.6;
		if (len < 2.0 || str <= 0.01) { BladeGlowOff(); return; }
		GlowTunables();                     // once a tic, never inside GlowPredict
		// ubqs_beam_shift: where along the blade's line the WORLD BEAM starts, for fitting a hilt that is not
		// Wardust's. It is applied HERE and nowhere else -- deliberately NOT in BladeBase(), which is the
		// origin of the cut line (CutAlong), the blade-on-blade contact line (Clash), the block and deflect
		// origin and the dynamic lights. A look slider must not move where the blade cuts. Both base and
		// pommel move together, so the overlap room below and the back blade's offset are unchanged.
		// Note: ubqs_diag 2's telemetry computes the base without the shift, so with a shift set it reports
		// exactly that many units of base error -- which is the truth: the beam IS that far off the blade line.
		double shift = clamp(UF("ubqs_beam_shift", 0.0), -8.0, 8.0);
		if (shift != 0.0) { base += dir * shift; pom += dir * shift; }
		// THE PREDICTION WAS ALREADY DONE THIS TIC, ON THE HAND, IN PoseTick -- never here. GlowPredict keeps
		// a rolling three-sample history (gT0..gT2 / gB0..gB2 / gD0..gD2) plus one hysteresis bit; call it
		// twice in a tic -- once for the hilt and once for the emitter, which is what the obvious version of
		// this change does -- and the second call pushes the FIRST call's extrapolation in as a fresh sample,
		// so the velocity it measures and the lead it applies both COMPOUND, and the saber runs away on fast
		// swings. So it is called once, on the hand, which is the one thing the hilt and the beam both hang
		// off. The emitter is RIGID on it -- EmitAlong straight down the blade -- so it is DERIVED from that
		// one answer here instead of predicted again. That is what makes the hilt the player now sees and this
		// beam physically incapable of disagreeing (the owner, 10-01: "the blade detaches from the hilt when i
		// swing").
		// (snapQuiet and lastSizeIdx moved to PoseTick with the sample. lastSizeIdx has to be set even on the
		// tics the beam is off, because the ui telemetry reads it.)
		bool jump = gJump;
		bool sA = gSnapA, sL = gSnapL;
		Vector3 pDir = gPDir;
		Vector3 nDir = -pDir;
		Vector3 pb = owner.pos + gPRel + pDir * UBQS_Data.EmitAlong(SizeIdx());
		// the pommel rides the same hilt: as far down the (predicted) beam as it is down the real one
		Vector3 pp = pb + pDir * ((pom - base) dot dir);
		int ci = UInt("ubqs_blade_glow_color", -1);
		int col = (ci < 0) ? ColIdx() : clamp(ci, 0, UBQS_Data.NCOL - 1);
		// BUILD 51 (the owner: "far too fat"): the shells are built in world units at the film look (vgface.py:
		// white core out to ~0.33 = the emitter mouth, the colour tight round it, a faint bloom to 2.8), drawn 1:1
		// at ubqs_glow_width 1.2 -- its old default, so a saved setting keeps meaning "the designed width"
		double w = UF("ubqs_glow_width", 1.2) / 1.2 * UBQS_Data.Size(SizeIdx());
		int q = clamp(UInt("ubqs_glow_quality", 3), 1, 4);
		double a = clamp(str / 0.6, 0.0, 1.0);   // the capsule's profile is designed at alpha 1 = the default 0.6
		double fade = UInt("ubqs_glow_motionfade", 1) ? gFade : 0.0;
		// ubqs_glow_fade_widen: the other half of motionfade -- the halo widening that is supposed to read as
		// motion blur. It was an inline literal, and width is the thing he has called out twice.
		double ac = a * (1.0 - fade), wh = w * (1.0 + clamp(UF("ubqs_glow_fade_widen", 0.25), 0.0, 1.0) * fade);
		// THE BEAM REACHES THE HILT (build 54; the owner, 10-01: "give life to that beam thing"). Each
		// shell fades in over a length that grows with its radius (vgface.py), so AT the emitter mouth
		// the glow is only about 13% of full: measured off the shipped meshes with tools/joint51vs52.py,
		// the core reaches full 0.5 units above the mouth and the halo 1.5. That dim band is a dark gap
		// between the hilt and where the beam becomes visible -- it is there with ZERO prediction error,
		// and it is why the beam looks detached even standing still. Start each part its OWN fade-in
		// length below the mouth and lengthen it to match, so the tip does not move and each part is at
		// full strength exactly where it leaves the hilt, with only its faint taper behind.
		// Per part: the halo blooms to 2.8 units against a hilt of 0.62, so a halo overlap big enough to
		// matter sleeves the hilt in light (tried at 4 units; it swallowed the hilt).
		double room = -((pom - base) dot dir);
		double cap = room * (back ? 0.45 : 0.9);
		double ovC = clamp(min(UF("ubqs_glow_overlap_core", 0.5), cap), 0.0, 4.0);
		double ovH = clamp(min(UF("ubqs_glow_overlap_halo", 1.5), cap), 0.0, 4.0);
		gHalo = UBQS_BeamGlow.Put(gHalo, false, pb - pDir * ovH, pDir, len + ovH, wh, col, q, a, jump, sA, sL);
		gCore = UBQS_BeamGlow.Put(gCore, true, pb - pDir * ovC, pDir, len + ovC, w, col, q, ac, jump, sA, sL);
		if (back)
		{
			gHaloB = UBQS_BeamGlow.Put(gHaloB, false, pp + pDir * ovH, nDir, len + ovH, wh, col, q, a, jump, sA, sL);
			gCoreB = UBQS_BeamGlow.Put(gCoreB, true, pp + pDir * ovC, nDir, len + ovC, w, col, q, ac, jump, sA, sL);
		}
		else
		{
			if (gHaloB) gHaloB.Destroy();
			if (gCoreB) gCoreB.Destroy();
			gHaloB = null;
			gCoreB = null;
		}
		GlowDots(pb, pDir, len, pp, jump || sA || sL);
	}
	// THE SOFT GLOWING DOTS INSIDE THE BLADE (build 48's look), now optional (ubqs_glow_dots) and on the
	// same predicted pose as the shell
	private void GlowDots(Vector3 base, Vector3 dir, double len, Vector3 pom, bool jump)
	{
		int N = 10;
		double str = 0.42;
		int want = UInt("ubqs_glow_dots", 0) ? (back ? N * 2 : N) : 0;
		while (bglow.Size() > want) { let g = bglow[bglow.Size() - 1]; if (g) g.Destroy(); bglow.Pop(); }
		if (want == 0) return;
		int rgb = UBQS_Data.Mix(RgbNow(), 0xFFFFFF, 0.15);
		double sc = 0.17;
		for (int i = 0; i < want; i++)
		{
			int k = i % N;
			double t = 0.05 + 0.10 * k;
			Vector3 at = (i < N) ? base + dir * (len * t) : pom - dir * (len * t);
			bool fresh = i >= bglow.Size();
			if (fresh) bglow.Push(UBQS_FX.Fx(at, 'UXGL', 1, 1000, sc, str, rgb));
			let g = bglow[i];
			if (!g) continue;
			g.SetOrigin(at, true);
			if (jump || fresh) g.ClearInterpolation();
			g.life = g.total;
			g.scale = (sc, sc);
			g.a0 = str * (k == N - 1 ? 0.7 : 1.0);
			g.SetShade(rgb);
		}
	}
	private void BladeGlowOff()
	{
		for (int i = 0; i < bglow.Size(); i++) if (bglow[i]) bglow[i].Destroy();
		bglow.Clear();
		if (gCore) gCore.Destroy();
		if (gHalo) gHalo.Destroy();
		if (gCoreB) gCoreB.Destroy();
		if (gHaloB) gHaloB.Destroy();
		gCore = null;
		gHalo = null;
		gCoreB = null;
		gHaloB = null;
		// NOT gN / gStill any more. The motion history belongs to the HILT as well now (PoseTick), and the
		// hilt is drawn whenever the saber is in your hand -- doused, blade retracted, ubqs_blade_glow 0 --
		// so wiping it here would make the hilt JUMP on every one of those tics instead of sliding, which is a
		// 35 Hz staircase on an opaque object in your hand. PoseTick's PoseForget() forgets it when the saber
		// really LEAVES the hand or starts a twirl, which are the only moments it is actually stale, and a
		// beam coming back spawns fresh actors, which forces its own jump inside Put().
	}

	// ---- THE SWING TRAIL: the path the blade swept this tic, filled with fading glow (particles, no light) ----
	private void Trail(Vector3 base, Vector3 tip, double speed, double cut)
	{
		// Soft glows of the blade's colour along the arc it swept, evenly spaced: one blob pair at the cut
		// threshold and one more for every 8 units a tic above it, up to ubqs_trail_steps. The ramp is
		// measured from `cut` and not from a bare 8, so the two cannot drift apart -- and at the shipped cap
		// of 2 this is bit-identical to the old `clamp(int(speed / 8.0), 1, 2)` at every speed.
		// The CAP is what the slider sets, and the whole of its range is reachable on a real swing: 2 blobs at
		// cut + 8 units a tic, 3 at cut + 16, 4 at cut + 24. The mod's own idea of a hard swing (where the
		// whoosh saturates) is 24, so 4 is a genuinely hard arc and not a number he can never see.
		// ubqs_trail_life is the knob that turns dots into a streak; it is fully live over its whole range.
		int rgb = RgbNow();
		int most = clamp(UInt("ubqs_trail_steps", 2), 1, 4);
		int life = clamp(UInt("ubqs_trail_life", 6), 1, 24);
		int steps = clamp(1 + int((speed - cut) / 8.0), 1, most);
		for (int i = 0; i < steps; i++)
		{
			double s = (i + 0.5) / steps;
			Vector3 b = lastBase + (base - lastBase) * s;
			Vector3 e = lastTip + (tip - lastTip) * s;
			UBQS_Data.Glow(b + (e - b) * 0.6, rgb, 0.10, 0.4, life);
			UBQS_Data.Glow(b + (e - b) * 0.95, rgb, 0.12, 0.5, life);
		}
	}

	// ---- CUT: whatever the blade is in ------------------------------------------------------------------
	void CutAlong(double speed)
	{
		Vector3 hand = BladeBase(), dir = BladeDir();
		double len = BladeLen();
		// THE ARC THE BLADE ACTUALLY TRAVELLED, which is the direction a cut throws a body. Taken here,
		// before the history moves on, so it is the same step `speed` was measured from; the body's own
		// motion is already out of it, so walking into a monster does not shove it.
		Vector3 sw = lastOk ? (((hand + dir * len) - lastTip) - bodyStep) : (0, 0, 0);
		if (sw.Length() < 0.01) sw = dir;
		sw = sw.Unit();
		CutLine(hand, dir, len, speed, sw);
		if (back) CutLine(Pommel(), -dir, len, speed, sw);
	}
	private void CutLine(Vector3 base, Vector3 dir, double len, double speed, Vector3 sw)
	{
		if (len < 1) return;
		Vector3 mid = base + dir * (len * 0.5);
		double reach = len * 0.5 + 48.0;
		// EVERY SETTING IS READ HERE, ABOVE THE ITERATOR. UBQS_Data.F is an uncached CVar.GetCVar by string
		// name and this loop runs over every actor in the blade's box, so a read at a use site inside it is
		// unbounded. ubqs_cut_rate: how soon the SAME enemy can be cut again -- this, not ubqs_damage, is the
		// real cap on the saber's rate of killing, and the reason holding the blade inside a monster does not
		// delete it. ubqs_cut_pad: how near a miss still cuts. ubqs_swing_scale: how much swing speed changes
		// the damage (0 = not at all, which is what anyone seated or in a small room needs -- they live on the
		// 0.5 floor of this curve for good otherwise). Its slider stops at 1 because above 1 the floor drives
		// the product toward zero, and a cut that draws blood and plays a hit for no damage is worse than none.
		int    rate = max(UInt("ubqs_cut_rate", 8), 1);
		double pad  = UF("ubqs_cut_pad", 3.0);
		double dmg0 = UF("ubqs_damage", 30.0);
		double mult = 1.0 + (clamp(speed / 20.0, 0.5, 2.0) - 1.0) * clamp(UF("ubqs_swing_scale", 1.0), 0.0, 1.0);
		double vhit = UF("ubqs_vol_hit", 1.0);
		bool   buzzc = UInt("ubqs_haptic_cut", 1) != 0;
		double shove = UF("ubqs_cut_shove", 1.0);
		double lift  = clamp(UF("ubqs_cut_lift", 0.35), 0.0, 1.0);
		bool   los   = UInt("ubqs_cut_los", 1) != 0;
		bool   cutAny = false;
		let it = BlockThingsIterator.CreateFromPos(mid.x, mid.y, mid.z - reach, reach * 2.0, reach, false);
		while (it.Next())
		{
			Actor mo = it.thing;
			if (!mo || mo == owner || !mo.bShootable || mo.health <= 0) continue;
			if (mo.bFriendly && owner.player) continue;
			if (mo.player && !deathmatch) continue;
			int i = cutWho.Find(mo);
			if (i < cutWho.Size() && level.maptime - cutWhen[i] < rate) continue;
			Vector3 c = level.Vec3Diff(base, (mo.pos.xy, mo.pos.z + mo.height * 0.5));
			Vector3 blade = dir * len;
			double t = clamp((c dot blade) / (len * len), 0.0, 1.0);
			Vector3 gap = c - blade * t;
			if ((gap.xy).Length() > mo.radius + pad || abs(gap.z) > mo.height * 0.5 + pad) continue;
			// NOT THROUGH THE WALL. The iterator box is nearly 100 units across and nothing here ever
			// asked whether the blade could reach what it found, so a swing near a thin wall or a closed
			// door killed what was behind it. Paint() and GazeTarget() have always used this exact test;
			// only the cut never got it. Last of the per-victim tests, so it costs a sight check only for
			// something the blade geometrically touched.
			if (los && !owner.CheckSight(mo, SF_IGNOREVISIBILITY)) continue;
			int dmg = int(dmg0 * mult);
			Vector3 at = level.Vec3Offset(base, blade * t);
			CutFx(at, dir, mo, dmg);
			mo.DamageMobj(self, owner, dmg, 'Saber', DMG_THRUSTLESS);
			// ...AND IT MOVES WHAT IT CUT. The engine's own thrust cannot be used: the inflictor is this
			// Weapon item, which has no position of its own, which is what DMG_THRUSTLESS is for. So the
			// shove is ours, along the arc, scaled by the victim's MASS (an imp is 100, a Cyberdemon 1000)
			// and by the same swing-speed multiplier the damage uses. The lift is what makes it read as a
			// stagger instead of a slide: a Doom monster off the floor cannot change direction.
			if (mo && !mo.bDestroyed && shove > 0.01 && !mo.bDontThrust && !mo.bNoDamageThrust)
			{
				double kk = shove * 5.0 * clamp(100.0 / max(mo.mass, 1.0), 0.08, 2.0) * mult;
				mo.vel += sw * kk;
				mo.vel.z += kk * lift;
			}
			UBQS_Ping.At(owner, at, mo.bNoBlood ? "ubqs/wall" : "ubqs/hit", vhit);
			FlashAt(at, 56, 3);
			cutAny = true;
			if (i < cutWho.Size()) cutWhen[i] = level.maptime;
			else { cutWho.Push(mo); cutWhen.Push(level.maptime); }
		}
		// THE BLADE GOING THROUGH A BODY is the single event a VR player most expects to feel, and it did
		// nothing: all five Buzz() sites were Force or targeting events. ONCE per swing, not once per victim --
		// a sweep through four imps is one pulse a controller could tell apart, and Buzz() is a LineAttack.
		// Off by default, so today is unchanged -- but this is the first thing to turn on (ubqs_haptic_cut).
		if (buzzc && cutAny) Rumble(0.9, 4);
		for (int k = cutWho.Size() - 1; k >= 0; k--)
			if (!cutWho[k] || cutWho[k].health <= 0) { cutWho.Delete(k); cutWhen.Delete(k); }
	}

	// WHAT A LIGHTSABER LEAVES BEHIND (the owner, 10-02: "we don't have anyb kind of 'cut the monster'
	// effects, no sparks, nothin, no smoke, nothin").
	// He was right, and for two reasons that both look like working code. The entry flash was UXHF at
	// scale 0.12 -- on a 96-pixel sprite that is nine pixels, invisible beside the blade's own glow. And
	// UBQS_Data.Sparks sat in the `else` for bNoBlood actors, which no monster is: the CombatFX spark
	// burst was already shipped in this pack and no kill had ever fired it. Smoke was simply absent.
	// A cut does not bleed, it cauterizes. So: a white-hot flash in the blade's colour where the beam
	// goes in, the spark burst thrown back the way the blade came, and smoke off the wound -- RS_Main's
	// JSMO blast smoke (UXPD, already in the pack for the Force push), non-additive, not bright, drifting
	// up. The smoke is the one that reads as burnt meat, and it is the one that was missing.
	// Everything scales with the victim (radius 20 is an imp, 40 a Cyberdemon) and with ubqs_cut_fx, so it
	// turns down without touching the damage.
	private void CutFx(Vector3 at, Vector3 dir, Actor mo, int dmg)
	{
		if (!mo.bNoBlood) mo.SpawnBlood(at, VectorAngle(dir.x, dir.y), dmg);
		double k = clamp(UF("ubqs_cut_fx", 1.0), 0.0, 3.0);
		if (k <= 0.01) return;
		int rgb = RgbNow();
		double bs = clamp(mo.radius / 20.0, 0.6, 2.2);
		UBQS_FX.Fx(at, 'UXHF', 10, 1, 0.30 * bs * k, 0.85, UBQS_Data.Mix(rgb, 0xFFFFFF, 0.45));
		UBQS_FX.Fx(at, 'UXST', 1, 5, 0.07 * bs * k, 0.90, -1, 0.90);
		UBQS_Data.Sparks(at, -dir, rgb, int(clamp(7.0 * bs, 4.0, 14.0)));
		// three puffs, each its own size and its own way up, so the smoke has some body instead of being
		// one sprite sitting in the air
		for (int s = 0; s < 3; s++)
		{
			Vector3 p = at + (frandom[UBQSFx](-1.0, 1.0) * mo.radius * 0.3,
			                  frandom[UBQSFx](-1.0, 1.0) * mo.radius * 0.3,
			                  frandom[UBQSFx](0.0, 5.0));
			UBQS_FX.Fx(p, 'UXPD', 18, 2, (0.11 + 0.045 * s) * bs * k, 0.55, -1, 1.035, false,
				(frandom[UBQSFx](-0.22, 0.22), frandom[UBQSFx](-0.22, 0.22), frandom[UBQSFx](0.30, 0.75)),
				true);
		}
	}

	// ---- THE TWIRLING STAFF: a disc of blade, as wide as the blade is long, square to your hand's aim ---------
	private void TwirlDisc(Vector3 hand, double len)
	{
		if (len < 4) return;
		Vector3 n = Aim();
		double reach = len + 160.0;
		// read above the iterator, as in CutLine. ubqs_cut_rate is the SAME cvar the swing uses, so the two
		// cooldowns cannot drift apart; ubqs_dmg_twirl is the disc's own share of ubqs_damage (a bare 0.8).
		int    rate = max(UInt("ubqs_cut_rate", 8), 1);
		double dmg0 = UF("ubqs_damage", 30.0) * UF("ubqs_dmg_twirl", 0.8);
		double vhit = UF("ubqs_vol_hit", 1.0);
		let it = BlockThingsIterator.CreateFromPos(hand.x, hand.y, hand.z - reach, reach * 2.0, reach, false);
		while (it.Next())
		{
			Actor mo = it.thing;
			if (!mo || mo == owner) continue;
			Vector3 c = level.Vec3Diff(hand, mo.pos);
			if (mo.bMissile)
			{
				if (mo.target == owner || mo is "UBQS_Thrown" || !UInt("ubqs_deflect", 1)) continue;
				// where its path this tic crosses the disc's plane, and whether that is inside the disc
				double a0 = c dot n, a1 = (c + mo.vel) dot n;
				if ((a0 > 0) == (a1 > 0) && min(abs(a0), abs(a1)) > mo.radius + 4.0) continue;
				double t = (abs(a0 - a1) > 0.001) ? clamp(a0 / (a0 - a1), 0.0, 1.0) : 0.0;
				Vector3 hit = c + mo.vel * t;
				if ((hit - n * (hit dot n)).Length() > len + mo.radius) continue;
				BatBack(mo, n);
				continue;
			}
			if (!mo.bShootable || mo.health <= 0 || (mo.bFriendly && owner.player) || (mo.player && !deathmatch)) continue;
			Vector3 mid = c + (0, 0, mo.height * 0.5);
			double along = mid dot n;
			if (abs(along) > mo.radius + 6.0) continue;
			if ((mid - n * along).Length() > len + mo.radius) continue;
			int i = cutWho.Find(mo);
			if (i < cutWho.Size() && level.maptime - cutWhen[i] < rate) continue;
			int dmg = int(dmg0);
			Vector3 at = level.Vec3Offset(hand, mid);
			if (!mo.bNoBlood) mo.SpawnBlood(at, VectorAngle(n.x, n.y), dmg);
			mo.DamageMobj(self, owner, dmg, 'Saber', DMG_THRUSTLESS);
			UBQS_Ping.At(owner, at, mo.bNoBlood ? "ubqs/wall" : "ubqs/hit", vhit);
			if (i < cutWho.Size()) cutWhen[i] = level.maptime;
			else { cutWho.Push(mo); cutWhen.Push(level.maptime); }
		}
	}

	// ---- DEFLECT: a missile crossing the blade -- where it is now, where it was a tic ago, or between -------
	// The blade moves several units a tic when swung, so testing only where it is now lets fast bolts slip
	// through a fast swing. Three samples of the swept blade against the bolt's whole path this tic.
	void Deflect(Vector3 base, Vector3 dir, double len)
	{
		if (len < 1) return;
		Vector3 mid = base + dir * (len * 0.5);
		double reach = len * 0.5 + 300.0;          // fast bolts cover a lot of ground in a tic (two tics ahead)
		Vector3 pb = lastOk ? lastBase : base;
		Vector3 pt = lastOk ? lastTip : base + dir * len;
		// ubqs_deflect_lead: how far along a shot's OWN path the blade is tested, in tics. 3 is what fixed his
		// report that one blade held across did not turn Wardust's fast bolts -- and it is also why shots are
		// turned two tics early, including ones that would have missed. Only he can say whether that now feels
		// psychic. Read above the loop, not inside it.
		double dlead = clamp(UF("ubqs_deflect_lead", 3.0), 1.0, 6.0);
		let it = BlockThingsIterator.CreateFromPos(mid.x, mid.y, mid.z - reach, reach * 2.0, reach, false);
		while (it.Next())
		{
			Actor mo = it.thing;
			if (!mo || !mo.bMissile || mo == owner || mo.target == owner || mo is "UBQS_Thrown") continue;
			double near = 1e9;
			for (int k = 0; k <= 2; k++)
			{
				double t = k * 0.5;
				Vector3 b = pb + (base - pb) * t;
				Vector3 e = pt + ((base + dir * len) - pt) * t;
				// the shot's path from a tic back to two tics ahead: Wardust's bolts are fast enough to go from in
				// front of the blade to inside you between two checks (the owner, 10-01: one blade, held across,
				// did not deflect)
				near = min(near, UBQS_Data.SegSeg(level.Vec3Diff(b, mo.pos - mo.vel), mo.vel * dlead, e - b));
			}
			if (near > mo.radius + 5.0) continue;
			BatBack(mo, dir);
		}
	}

	// WHERE A DEFLECTED SHOT GOES (ubqs_deflect_aim): 0 back at whoever fired it; 1 where you are LOOKING,
	// helped onto the nearest enemy inside a narrow cone of your gaze; 2 straight off the blade, a mirror.
	void BatBack(Actor mo, Vector3 blade)
	{
		Actor shooter = mo.target;
		double sp = max(mo.Speed, mo.vel.Length()) * 1.2;
		if (sp <= 0) sp = 12;
		Vector3 d = (0, 0, 0);
		int aim = UInt("ubqs_deflect_aim", 1);
		if (aim == 1)
		{
			// ubqs_deflect_assist: the aim help that puts a deflected shot onto an enemy. It happens to equal
			// ubqs_lock_cone's default, which makes it LOOK linked to it -- it is not, and turning
			// ubqs_lock_cone does nothing here. 0 = hard-mode deflection, with no help at all.
			double gcone = UF("ubqs_deflect_assist", 14.0);
			Actor pick = null;
			if (gcone > 0.0) pick = GazeTarget(gcone);
			if (pick) d = level.Vec3Diff(mo.pos, (pick.pos.xy, pick.pos.z + pick.height * 0.55));
			else d = (cos(owner.angle) * cos(owner.pitch), sin(owner.angle) * cos(owner.pitch), -sin(owner.pitch));
		}
		else if (aim == 2)
		{
			Vector3 v = mo.vel.Unit();
			Vector3 n = (blade cross (v cross blade));
			if (n.Length() > 0.001) { n = n.Unit(); d = v - n * (2.0 * (v dot n)); }
		}
		if (d.Length() < 0.001 && shooter && shooter != owner && shooter.health > 0)
			d = level.Vec3Diff(mo.pos, (shooter.pos.xy, shooter.pos.z + shooter.height * 0.5));
		if (d.Length() < 0.001) d = -mo.vel;
		if (d.Length() < 0.001) d = (1, 0, 0);
		d = d.Unit();
		mo.target = owner;
		if (mo.bSeekerMissile) mo.tracer = shooter;
		mo.vel = d * sp;
		mo.angle = VectorAngle(d.x, d.y);
		mo.pitch = -asin(clamp(d.z, -1.0, 1.0));
		// ubqs_vol_clash covers the blade meeting energy, which is a deflect as much as a crossing: ubqs/deflect
		// is one of the most frequent combat sounds in the mod (ubqs_deflect is on by default) and had no knob
		// at all. All three of its sites read the one cvar.
		owner.A_StartSound(UBQS_Font.Clash(), CHAN_AUTO, 0, UF("ubqs_vol_clash", 1.0));
		UBQS_Data.Sparks(mo.pos, d, RgbNow(), 8);
		FlashAt(mo.pos, 64, 4);
	}

	// THE ENEMY YOU ARE LOOKING AT: the nearest live one inside `cone` degrees of your gaze, that you can see.
	Actor GazeTarget(double cone)
	{
		Vector3 eye = owner.Vec3Offset(0, 0, owner.player ? owner.player.viewheight : 41.0);
		Vector3 look = (cos(owner.angle) * cos(owner.pitch), sin(owner.angle) * cos(owner.pitch), -sin(owner.pitch));
		Actor best = null;
		double bestScore = 1e9;
		let it = BlockThingsIterator.CreateFromPos(eye.x, eye.y, eye.z - 1536, 3072, 1536, false);
		while (it.Next())
		{
			Actor mo = it.thing;
			if (!mo || !mo.bIsMonster || mo.health <= 0 || mo.bFriendly || mo == owner) continue;
			Vector3 to = level.Vec3Diff(eye, (mo.pos.xy, mo.pos.z + mo.height * 0.55));
			double dist = to.Length();
			if (dist < 1 || dist > 1536) continue;
			double off = acos(clamp((to / dist) dot look, -1.0, 1.0));
			if (off > cone) continue;
			if (!owner.CheckSight(mo, SF_IGNOREVISIBILITY)) continue;
			double score = off * 40.0 + dist * 0.05;
			if (score < bestScore) { bestScore = score; best = mo; }
		}
		return best;
	}

	// IS THE BLADE ACTUALLY IN THE WAY? (ubqs_blade_guard.) The attack's line -- from the attacker's
	// middle to yours -- against the blade's own segment, closest approach, in map units. `w` is how far
	// off the blade's line still counts: the blade is about 26 units long at size 1 and your body is 32
	// across, so 6 makes a slab roughly a quarter of your silhouette. Small enough that putting it there
	// is a decision, big enough to survive a 35Hz sample of a moving arm.
	// NOTHING HERE ASKS WHETHER THE BLADE IS HORIZONTAL. Held across your chest it crosses the line and
	// blocks; held pointing forward it is edge-on to the line and blocks nothing. That falls out of the
	// geometry, which is the whole reason it will feel real instead of feeling like a dice roll.
	// The pommel blade counts too, when the hilt has one lit.
	private bool BladeInPath(Actor source, double w)
	{
		if (!owner || !source) return false;
		Vector3 from = (source.pos.xy, source.pos.z + source.height * 0.5);
		Vector3 db = level.Vec3Diff(from, (owner.pos.xy, owner.pos.z + owner.height * 0.5));
		if (db.Length() < 1.0) return false;
		double len = BladeLen();
		if (len < 1.0) return false;
		Vector3 dir = BladeDir();
		// SegSeg's frame (see UBQS_Data.SegVec): segment A as (its start RELATIVE to B's start, its
		// vector), segment B as its vector from that start. A is the blade, B is the shot.
		if (UBQS_Data.SegSeg(level.Vec3Diff(from, BladeBase()), dir * len, db) <= w) return true;
		if (back && UBQS_Data.SegSeg(level.Vec3Diff(from, Pommel()), -dir * len, db) <= w) return true;
		return false;
	}

	// ---- BLOCK: a hitscan shot (a trooper's rifle, a zombie's pistol) stopped by a lit blade facing it ------
	// Missiles are the deflect's; melee is not blocked. A blade swung in the last third of a second always
	// blocks; held still, ubqs_block percent of the time. A blocked shot can go back (ubqs_block_return).
	override void ModifyDamage(int damage, Name damageType, out int newdamage, bool passive, Actor inflictor, Actor source, int flags)
	{
		if (!passive || damage <= 0 || !owner) return;
		// THE CROSS GUARD (your two blades crossed in front of you, an X or a +): NOTHING from in front gets
		// through -- shots, bolts, claws, blasts. From behind, it does not help.
		if (Guarding())
		{
			Actor from = inflictor ? inflictor : source;
			if (from && from != owner)
			{
				double off = abs(DeltaAngle(owner.angle, VectorAngle(from.pos.x - owner.pos.x, from.pos.y - owner.pos.y)));
				// ubqs_guard_arc: 100 either side is 200 degrees of TOTAL immunity, measured from the BODY's
				// yaw and not from the blades. The most abusable number in the mod, with no way to tighten it.
				// ubqs_guard_arc is the outer gate: nothing from behind you is guarded, whatever the blades
				// are doing. ubqs_guard_width is the wall itself -- ONE of the two crossed blades has to be
				// in the attack's own path, exactly as the single-blade block is tested, just wider, because
				// an X is a big object and a lock is held with a trembling hand. 0 is the old arc alone.
				// This is what makes WHERE you cross them matter.
				double gw2 = clamp(UF("ubqs_guard_width", 14.0), 0.0, 48.0);
				let og = Other();
				bool inPath = gw2 <= 0.01 || BladeInPath(from, gw2) || (og && og.BladeInPath(from, gw2));
				if (off < UF("ubqs_guard_arc", 100.0) && inPath)
				{
					newdamage = 0;
					owner.A_StartSound(UBQS_Font.Clash(), CHAN_AUTO, 0, UF("ubqs_vol_clash", 1.0));
					double gfx = clamp(UF("ubqs_clash_fx", 1.0), 0.0, 3.0);
					if (gfx > 0.01)
					{
						UBQS_ClashFlash.Burst(guardAt, 0.8 * gfx);
						UBQS_Data.Sparks(guardAt, (0, 0, 1), 0xFFFFFF, int(8 * gfx));
						FlashAt(guardAt, 80 * gfx, 3);
					}
					return;
				}
			}
		}
		if (!Lit() || !source || source == owner) return;
		if (inflictor && inflictor.bMissile) return;        // missiles are the deflect's: it bats them back
		// ONE SABER, HELD ACROSS YOU (ubqs_blade_guard -- the owner, 10-02: "one saber, hosiztonally, with a
		// small ass hitbox to be kinda tralistic"). The cross guard above is an ARC off the BODY's yaw and
		// stops everything inside it. This is its opposite: the blade's own segment against the attack's own
		// line, no cone and no dice, so where you hold the blade is the whole of it.
		// IT REPLACES THE ROLL, it does not stack on it. The roll below is 70 per cent of everything inside
		// 150 degrees of the blade's aim, which swamps any amount of precision -- a geometric guard layered
		// over it would be unfeelable. ubqs_blade_guard 0 is exactly the old behaviour, roll and all.
		// The roll also bailed out inside 96 units, so a claw was never blocked by anything but the cross
		// guard. The geometric path has no distance floor: a blade across you stops a claw, which is right.
		double gw = clamp(UF("ubqs_blade_guard", 6.0), 0.0, 24.0);
		if (gw > 0.01)
		{
			if (!BladeInPath(source, gw)) return;
		}
		else
		{
			if (owner.Distance3D(source) < 96) return;
			Vector3 aim = Aim();
			double toShooter = VectorAngle(source.pos.x - owner.pos.x, source.pos.y - owner.pos.y);
			if (abs(DeltaAngle(VectorAngle(aim.x, aim.y), toShooter)) > UF("ubqs_block_cone", 75.0)) return;
			// ubqs_block_swung: inside this window ubqs_block is ignored entirely and EVERY hitscan is blocked.
			// A third of a second of total immunity after any fast swing -- and the twirl sets lastFastTic
			// every single tic, so a twirling player never leaves it. 0 turns the window off.
			bool swung = level.maptime - lastFastTic < UInt("ubqs_block_swung", 12);
			if (!swung && random[UBQSBlock](1, 100) > UInt("ubqs_block", 70)) return;
		}
		newdamage = 0;
		Vector3 hand = BladeBase(), dir = BladeDir();
		Vector3 at = hand + dir * (BladeLen() * 0.6);
		Vector3 back = level.Vec3Diff(at, (source.pos.xy, source.pos.z + source.height * 0.55));
		if (back.Length() > 0.001) back = back.Unit();
		BlockFx(at, back, source, damage, true);
	}

	// ---- THE PARRY: the blade going INTO the shot, not merely standing in it --------------------
	// The blade's own step this tic (the body's motion out of it, as everywhere else) against the
	// direction the shot was travelling. 1.0 is a block; above it is a parry. Nothing is latched and
	// nothing is remembered: it is the step that is happening when the shot arrives, which is what the
	// player felt themselves do. ubqs_parry_speed is in the SAME units as ubqs_swing_cut.
	double ParryGain(Vector3 shotDir)
	{
		if (!lastOk) return 1.0;
		double need = UF("ubqs_parry_speed", 6.0);
		if (need <= 0.01 || shotDir.Length() < 0.001) return 1.0;
		Vector3 step = ((BladeBase() + BladeDir() * BladeLen()) - lastTip) - bodyStep;
		double sp = step.Length();
		if (sp < need) return 1.0;
		Vector3 su = step / sp;
		Vector3 sd = shotDir.Unit();
		double into = -(su dot sd);
		if (into < 0.3) return 1.0;
		return 1.0 + (clamp(UF("ubqs_parry_power", 2.0), 1.0, 4.0) - 1.0) * clamp(into, 0.0, 1.0);
	}

	// THE BLOCK'S NOISE, SPARKS, FLASH AND RETURN BOLT, in one place because two callers make it now:
	// ModifyDamage, which sees a shot that already hit, and StopsHitscan, which sees one before it is
	// traced at all. `loud` is false for the second and later pellets of one shotgun blast in a tic.
	int lastBlockTic;
	void BlockFx(Vector3 at, Vector3 back, Actor src, int damage, bool loud)
	{
		if (!owner) return;
		double pg = ParryGain(-back);
		if (loud)
		{
			UBQS_Ping.At(owner, at, UBQS_Font.Clash(), UF("ubqs_vol_clash", 1.0), pg > 1.01 ? 1.25 : 1.0);
			Rumble(0.8 * pg, pg > 1.01 ? 5 : 3);
		}
		UBQS_Data.Sparks(at, back, RgbNow(), int(10 * pg));
		FlashAt(at, 64 * pg, 4);
		if (!loud || !UInt("ubqs_block_return", 1)) return;
		Vector3 d = back;
		if (src && src.health > 0)
		{
			Vector3 toSrc = level.Vec3Diff(at, (src.pos.xy, src.pos.z + src.height * 0.55));
			if (toSrc.Length() > 0.001) d = toSrc.Unit();
		}
		let b = UBQS_Bolt(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_Bolt", at));
		if (!b) return;
		b.target = owner;
		b.rgb = RgbNow();
		b.vel = d * (b.Speed * pg);
		b.angle = VectorAngle(d.x, d.y);
		b.pitch = -asin(clamp(d.z, -1.0, 1.0));
	}

	// ---- A SHOT STOPPED AT THE MUZZLE, not in your chest ----------------------------------------
	// ModifyDamage can only ever block what was already going to hit you, tested against one line
	// drawn to your middle with a few units of slack -- so it blocked shots that would have missed and
	// missed shots that were really coming, and nothing the blade stood in front of but which was not
	// aimed at your centre could be stopped at all. This is the same block made BEFORE the engine
	// traces the bullet, against the shot's OWN ray, which WorldHitscanPreFired hands us exactly. A
	// blade really in the way stops it; one that is not, does not.
	bool StopsHitscan(Actor sh, Vector3 from, Vector3 dir, double dist, int damage)
	{
		if (!Lit() || !owner || owner.health <= 0 || owner == sh || !sh) return false;
		double gw = clamp(UF("ubqs_blade_guard", 6.0), 0.0, 24.0);
		if (gw <= 0.01) return false;
		double len = BladeLen();
		if (len < 1.0) return false;
		Vector3 mid = (owner.pos.xy, owner.pos.z + owner.height * 0.5);
		Vector3 toMe = level.Vec3Diff(from, mid);
		if ((toMe dot dir) <= 0) return false;		// it is not coming our way at all
		Vector3 ray = dir * max(dist, 1.0);
		double s, t, bs, bt;
		Vector3 sep = UBQS_Data.SegST(level.Vec3Diff(from, BladeBase()), BladeDir() * len, ray, s, t);
		bool got = sep.Length() <= gw;
		if (!got && back)
		{
			sep = UBQS_Data.SegST(level.Vec3Diff(from, Pommel()), -BladeDir() * len, ray, bs, bt);
			if (sep.Length() <= gw) { got = true; t = bt; }
		}
		if (!got) return false;
		// and it has to be stopped IN FRONT of us, not caught on its way to something behind us
		if ((ray * t).Length() > toMe.Length() + owner.radius * 2.0) return false;
		Vector3 at = level.Vec3Offset(from, ray * t);
		BlockFx(at, -dir, sh, damage, level.maptime != lastBlockTic);
		lastBlockTic = level.maptime;
		return true;
	}

	// ---- BURN: a blade pushed into a wall or the floor spits sparks and scorches it ----------------------
	private void Burn(Vector3 base, Vector3 dir, double len)
	{
		if (len < 4 || !UInt("ubqs_burn", 1)) return;
		let tr = new("UBQS_Tracer");
		Sector sec = level.PointInSector(base.xy);
		if (!tr.Trace(base, sec, dir, len, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, true)) return;
		if (tr.Results.HitType == TRACE_HitNone || tr.Results.HitType == TRACE_HitActor) return;
		Vector3 at = tr.Results.HitPos;
		if (burnQuiet > 0) return;
		burnQuiet = 5;
		UBQS_Ping.At(owner, at, "ubqs/burn", 0.7);
		if (tr.Results.HitType != TRACE_HitWall) return;
		// the scorch, sprayed from a hair in front of the wall (the flash light's actor, parked there dark)
		if (!flash) flash = UBQS_Light(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_Light", at - dir * 4.0));
		if (!flash) return;
		flash.SetOrigin(at - dir * 4.0, false);
		flash.A_SprayDecal("UBQS_Burn", 16.0, (0, 0, 0), dir);
		UBQS_FX.Fx(at - dir * 1.5, 'UXEM', 1, 18, 0.14, 0.8, -1, 0.97);
	}

	// ---- CLASH: your two blades crossing -------------------------------------------------------------------
	// THE BLADES CROSSING, as at the end of Empire. FIRST CONTACT: Jedi Academy's blade-on-blade hit over an
	// electric crack, a white-hot starburst, a crack of light, sparks -- harder the faster they met. HELD
	// TOGETHER (a blade lock): a looping electric snarl, bursts and a flickering light every couple of tics, and a
	// fresh snap now and then -- until you pull them apart. Contact is entered at 3 units and left only past 7
	// (or after 4 tics apart), so a lock does not stutter in and out on a trembling hand.
	bool inLock;
	int guardUntil;
	Vector3 guardAt;
	int lockSince, lastTouch, nextSnap;
	Vector3 otherLastTip;
	double lastSide;
	bool sideOk;
	bool Guarding() { return !bOffhandWeapon && level.maptime <= guardUntil && UInt("ubqs_crossguard", 1); }
	// THE CROSSING'S LIGHT (the owner, 10-01, Empire's carbon-freeze fight: "a nice flash of light to obscure
	// the geometry of the blades overlapping"): a hot white core where the beams pass through each other, in
	// a halo of both blades' colours -- two soft CombatFX glows that stay on while the blades are together,
	// steady (no flicker), swelling on the first hit and settling. Gone the moment they part.
	UBQS_FX lockCore, lockHalo;
	double glowPop;
	private void LockGlow(Vector3 at, int orgb)
	{
		if (!lockCore) lockCore = UBQS_FX.Fx(at, 'UXGL', 1, 1000, 0.2, 0.95, 0xFFFFFF);
		if (!lockHalo) lockHalo = UBQS_FX.Fx(at, 'UXGL', 1, 1000, 0.45, 0.5, UBQS_Data.Mix(UBQS_Data.Mix(RgbNow(), orgb, 0.5), 0xFFFFFF, 0.25));
		double k = 1.0 + glowPop;
		glowPop *= 0.8;
		if (lockCore)
		{
			lockCore.SetOrigin(at, true);
			lockCore.life = lockCore.total;
			lockCore.scale = (0.2, 0.2) * k;
			lockCore.roll = 0;
		}
		if (lockHalo)
		{
			lockHalo.SetOrigin(at, true);
			lockHalo.life = lockHalo.total;
			lockHalo.scale = (0.45, 0.45) * k;
			lockHalo.roll = 0;
		}
	}
	private void LockGlowOff()
	{
		if (lockCore) lockCore.Destroy();
		if (lockHalo) lockHalo.Destroy();
		lockCore = null;
		lockHalo = null;
	}
	private void EndLock()
	{
		LockGlowOff();
		if (!inLock) return;
		inLock = false;
		owner.A_StopSound(22);
	}
	private void Clash(Vector3 base, Vector3 dir, double len)
	{
		let o = Other();
		if (!o || len < 4 || o.Twirling()) { EndLock(); sideOk = false; return; }
		Vector3 ob = o.BladeBase(), od = o.BladeDir();
		double ol = o.BladeLen();
		if (ol < 4) { EndLock(); sideOk = false; return; }
		Vector3 otip = ob + od * ol;
		double rel = (lastOk ? ((otip - otherLastTip) - ((base + dir * len) - lastTip)).Length() : 0.0);
		otherLastTip = otip;
		// CONTACT, the same whichever blade is on top and at any angle (the owner, 10-01: only one + sparked).
		// Blades are a few units thick and the hand's pose is a tic old, so contact is generous -- and a blade
		// that went clean THROUGH the other between two tics (the side it is on flipped) counted as a hit too.
		Vector3 sep = UBQS_Data.SegVec(level.Vec3Diff(ob, base), dir * len, od * ol);
		double gap = sep.Length();
		Vector3 n = dir cross od;
		double side = 0;
		bool crossed = false;
		if (n.Length() > 0.15)
		{
			side = sep dot (n / n.Length());
			crossed = sideOk && gap < 14.0 && abs(lastSide) < 14.0 && ((side > 0) != (lastSide > 0));
		}
		lastSide = side;
		sideOk = n.Length() > 0.15;
		// NOT AT THE HANDLES (the owner, 10-01: "handles are still giving me some shit"): a touch whose nearest
		// point is within a hand's breadth of either emitter is the hilts bumping, not the beams crossing
		double sa, sb;
		UBQS_Data.SegST(level.Vec3Diff(ob, base), dir * len, od * ol, sa, sb);
		// ...and only when BOTH are down at their emitters (the owner, 10-01: with either one, the bottom third
		// of the blade went inert). One beam's base across the other's blade is a real crossing.
		// both tunable in game (the owner, 10-01): ubqs_contact, how close the beams must come; ubqs_contact_hilt,
		// the dead zone up from the emitters where hilts bumping is ignored
		double hz = UF("ubqs_contact_hilt", 0.75), cz = UF("ubqs_contact", 3.5);
		bool nearHilt = sa * len < hz && sb * ol < hz;
		// ubqs_lock_stick: contact is ENTERED at ubqs_contact and left only past this much of it. THIS
		// multiplier, not ubqs_contact, is what stops a lock stuttering in and out on a trembling hand, and it
		// is the only number that helps if he reports flickering locks. Floored at 1 in code. It is a `user`
		// cvar to sit with ubqs_contact and ubqs_contact_hilt, which are user today and reach the cross guard
		// the same way: the whole contact family is kept together rather than split down the middle.
		double stick = max(UF("ubqs_lock_stick", 1.7), 1.0);
		bool touching = !nearHilt && (crossed || gap <= (inLock ? cz * stick : cz));
		// == 1, NOT nonzero. ubqs_diag 2 is the glow telemetry overlay, and selecting it was also printing this
		// line every tic a blade lock was held. Fixed before ubqs_diag gets a menu row.
		if (UInt("ubqs_diag", 0) == 1) Console.Printf("ubqs clash gap %.1f side %.1f %s", gap, side, touching ? "HIT" : "");
		if (!touching)
		{
			LockGlowOff();
			if (inLock && level.maptime - lastTouch > 4) EndLock();
			return;
		}
		lastTouch = level.maptime;
		// WHERE THEY CROSS: halfway between the two blades' nearest points -- the crossing itself, wherever
		// along the blades it is (it was the point on this blade nearest the OTHER blade's middle, which
		// put the effect down at the hilts -- the owner, 10-01)
		Vector3 at = ((base + dir * (len * sa)) + (ob + od * (ol * sb))) * 0.5;
		// THE CROSS GUARD: blades held crossed, an X or a +, are a wall (ModifyDamage below)
		guardUntil = level.maptime + 2;
		guardAt = at;
		// ubqs_vol_clash scales the whole crossing together: the clash, the crack layered under it, and the
		// looping snarl with its swell. ubqs_clash_fx scales its sparks AND its flashes together (0 = none) --
		// including UBQS_ClashFlash.Burst and the lock's UXLT pulse, which are the most visible parts of a
		// clash, so "off" actually means off. One knob instead of six, and the cheapest way to trade spectacle
		// for frames. ubqs_haptic_clash buzzes on contact and keeps buzzing while the lock is held.
		// EVERY random[]/frandom[] CALL BELOW STAYS IN THE SHIPPED ORDER, drawn before the guard that might
		// skip the thing it feeds. The gating cvars are userinfo read off the owner, so every machine already
		// computes the same answer, but keeping the stream byte-identical costs nothing and removes the
		// question entirely.
		double vcl = UF("ubqs_vol_clash", 1.0);
		double cfx = clamp(UF("ubqs_clash_fx", 1.0), 0.0, 3.0);
		bool buzzk = UInt("ubqs_haptic_clash", 0) != 0;
		if (!inLock)
		{
			inLock = true;
			lockSince = level.maptime;
			nextSnap = level.maptime + random[UBQSFx](10, 18);
			double hard = clamp(rel / 12.0, 0.6, 1.6);
			owner.A_StartSound(UBQS_Font.Clash(), CHAN_AUTO, 0, 1.0 * vcl);
			owner.A_StartSound("ubqs/crack", CHAN_AUTO, 0, clamp(0.5 + hard * 0.3, 0.6, 1.0) * vcl);
			owner.A_StartSound(UBQS_Font.Lock(), 22, CHANF_LOOPING, 0.3 * vcl);
			if (cfx > 0.01)
			{
				UBQS_ClashFlash.Burst(at, hard * cfx);
				UBQS_Data.Sparks(at, (0, 0, 1), 0xFFFFFF, int(14 * hard * cfx));
				UBQS_Data.Sparks(at, (0, 0, 1), RgbNow(), int(6 * cfx));
				FlashAt(at, (80 + 30 * hard) * cfx, 4);
			}
			glowPop = 0.8 + 0.4 * hard;
			LockGlow(at, o.RgbNow());
			if (buzzk) Rumble(1.2, 3);
			return;
		}
		LockGlow(at, o.RgbNow());
		// THE LOCK: the snarl swells in as they stay together
		owner.A_SoundVolume(22, (0.3 + clamp((level.maptime - lockSince) / 10.0, 0.0, 1.0) * 0.6) * vcl);
		if ((level.maptime & 1) == 0)
		{
			double lsc = frandom[UBQSFx](0.2, 0.32);
			if (cfx > 0.01) UBQS_FX.Fx(at, 'UXLT', 4, 1, lsc, 0.9);
			bool spark = random[UBQSFx](0, 3) == 0;
			if (cfx > 0.01 && spark) UBQS_Data.Sparks(at, (0, 0, 1), 0xFFFFFF, int(4 * cfx));
			double lrad = frandom[UBQSFx](50, 96);
			if (cfx > 0.01) FlashAt(at, lrad * cfx, 2);
			if (buzzk) Rumble(1.2, 3);
		}
		if (level.maptime >= nextSnap)
		{
			nextSnap = level.maptime + random[UBQSFx](9, 20);
			owner.A_StartSound(UBQS_Font.Clash(), CHAN_AUTO, 0, 0.55 * vcl);
			owner.A_StartSound("ubqs/crack", CHAN_AUTO, 0, 0.5 * vcl);
			if (cfx > 0.01)
			{
				UBQS_ClashFlash.Burst(at, 1.0 * cfx);
				UBQS_Data.Sparks(at, (0, 0, 1), 0xFFFFFF, int(8 * cfx));
			}
		}
		// a hard knock while locked is a fresh clash
		if (rel > 14.0) { inLock = false; owner.A_StopSound(22); }
	}

	// ---- THE THROW -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	void Throw()
	{
		if (thrown || !owner) { ClearLocks(); return; }
		Vector3 hand = HandPos();
		let t = UBQS_Thrown(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_Thrown", hand));
		if (!t) { ClearLocks(); return; }
		t.target = owner;
		t.master = owner;
		t.launcher = self;
		t.col = ColIdx();
		// THE SECOND BLADE LIGHTS AS IT LEAVES YOUR HAND (ubqs_throw_double): a staff spinning is the throw
		t.dbl = back || UInt("ubqs_throw_double", 1);
		t.bladeLen = FullLen();
		for (int i = 0; i < locks.Size(); i++) if (locks[i]) t.route.Push(locks[i]);
		locks.Clear();
		// THE SPIN PLANE (ubqs_throw_plane): 0 your wrist decides -- thrown with the hand upright it goes end
		// over end, turned on its side it goes flat; 1 always flat; 2 always end over end
		int plane = UInt("ubqs_throw_plane", 0);
		double r = abs(HR());
		bool vert = (plane == 2) || (plane == 0 && (r < 45.0 || r > 135.0));
		// THE ARM'S OWN THROW: its speed and direction at the moment it let go. A hard throw flies fast and far,
		// along your swing (steadied toward where the hand points). Locked enemies are always flown to.
		Vector3 d = Aim();
		double flySpeed = 26.0, range = UF("ubqs_throw_range", 512.0);
		Vector3 hv = HandVel();
		double sp = hv.Length();
		// ubqs_throw_blend: how much of the throw is the direction the arm actually MOVED and how much is where
		// the hand points. 1 = all arm (honest), 0 = all aim (accurate) -- the classic VR slider.
		// ubqs_throw_speed multiplies the result, so it covers the still-hand base of 26 and the real-throw
		// clamp alike: the cosmetic spin was already a slider and the actual flight speed was not.
		if (t.route.Size() == 0 && sp > 0.5)
		{
			double bl = clamp(UF("ubqs_throw_blend", 0.6), 0.0, 1.0);
			d = (hv.Unit() * bl + d * (1.0 - bl)).Unit();
			flySpeed = clamp(16.0 + sp * 4.0, 22.0, 44.0);
			range *= clamp(sp / 4.0, 0.8, 1.6);
		}
		flySpeed *= clamp(UF("ubqs_throw_speed", 1.0), 0.5, 2.0);
		t.Speed = flySpeed;
		t.range = range;
		t.Launch(d, vert);
		thrown = t;
		Lights(false);
		owner.A_StartSound(UBQS_Font.Swing(), CHAN_WEAPON, 0, UF("ubqs_vol_swing", 1.0));
	}
	// BACK IN THE HAND: it lights again as it lands
	void Caught()
	{
		thrown = null;
		doused = false;
		ignited = true;
		igniteAnim = 0;
		if (owner)
		{
			owner.A_StartSound("ubqs/catch", CHAN_AUTO, 0, 0.8);
		}
	}

	// ---- LIGHT ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// ubqs_lights: 0 none; 1 QUEST -- one light per saber, mid-blade, and when your two blades are close
	// together only the main hand's lights them both; 2 two per blade; 3 three per blade (PC).
	// Every light is one attached light on a reused actor, moved, never respawned.
	private void Lights(bool on)
	{
		int mode = on ? UInt("ubqs_lights", 1) : 0;
		int want = clamp(mode, 0, 3);
		if (want == 1 && bOffhandWeapon)
		{
			let o = Other();
			if (o && (o.HandPos() - HandPos()).Length() < 40.0) want = 0;
		}
		while (glow.Size() > want)
		{
			let l = glow[glow.Size() - 1];
			if (l) l.Destroy();
			glow.Pop();
		}
		if (want == 0) return;
		Vector3 hand = HandPos(), dir = BladeDir();
		double len = BladeLen();
		hand = BladeBase();
		if (back) { Vector3 pm = Pommel(); double full = (hand + dir * len - (pm - dir * len)).Length(); hand = pm - dir * len; len = full; }   // a staff: the light runs the whole double blade
		int rgb = RgbNow();
		double rad = (want == 1) ? 26.0 + len * 0.85 : ((want == 2) ? 18.0 + len * 0.6 : 14.0 + len * 0.45);
		for (int k = 0; k < want; k++)
		{
			double t = (want == 1) ? 0.45 : ((want == 2) ? 0.25 + 0.5 * k : 0.15 + 0.35 * k);
			Vector3 at = hand + dir * (len * t);
			if (k >= glow.Size()) glow.Push(UBQS_Light(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_Light", at)));
			let l = glow[k];
			if (!l) continue;
			l.SetOrigin(at, true);
			l.Look(rgb, rad);
		}
	}
	// A SHORT FLASH: a hit, a block, a clash, a burn. One light, reused, a few tics.
	void FlashAt(Vector3 at, double rad, int tics)
	{
		// ubqs_flash: dropping ubqs_lights to 0 for frames silently took the hit, block, deflect, clash, guard
		// and burn flashes with it -- the player lost his combat FEEDBACK meaning only to lose the blade light,
		// and could not have one without the other. 1 (the default) is exactly as it shipped; 2 keeps the
		// flashes even with the blade light off; 0 drops them and keeps the light.
		int fl = UInt("ubqs_flash", 1);
		if (fl <= 0 || rad <= 0) return;
		if (fl == 1 && UInt("ubqs_lights", 1) <= 0) return;
		if (!flash) flash = UBQS_Light(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_Light", at));
		if (!flash) return;
		flash.SetOrigin(at, false);
		flash.Look(0xFFF0E0, rad);
		flashTics = max(flashTics, tics);
	}
	private void KillLights()
	{
		BladeGlowOff();
		// the hilt in the world goes with them, and the motion history with it: death, a weapon swap, the end
		// of a level. Nothing should ever slide in from the last place a destroyed saber was. This is also the
		// new home of the gN / gStill reset that BladeGlowOff used to do, because here it means what it says.
		PoseForget();
		for (int k = 0; k < glow.Size(); k++) if (glow[k]) glow[k].Destroy();
		glow.Clear();
		if (flash) flash.Destroy();
		flash = null;
		if (lockCore) lockCore.Destroy();
		if (lockHalo) lockHalo.Destroy();
	}
	override void OnDestroy()
	{
		KillLights();
		ClearLocks();
		// the two sound emitters are ours: nothing else will clean them up
		if (hummer) { hummer.Destroy(); hummer = null; }
		if (swish) { swish.Destroy(); swish = null; }
		if (thrown) thrown.Destroy();
		Super.OnDestroy();
	}
	override void DetachFromOwner()
	{
		KillLights();
		// the blade's hum emitter goes with the saber, or it is left humming in mid air
		HumOff();
		ignited = false;
		merged = false;
		Super.DetachFromOwner();
	}

	States
	{
	Spawn:
		UBPK A -1;
		Stop;
	Select:
		UBSP R 1 { A_UBShow(17); A_Raise(12); }
		Loop;
	Deselect:
		UBSP Q 1 { A_UBShow(16); A_UBOff(); }
		UBSP P 1 A_UBShow(15);
		UBSP O 1 A_UBShow(14);
		UBSP N 1 A_UBShow(13);
	DeselectLoop:
		UBSP R 1 { A_UBShow(17); A_Lower(12); }
		Loop;
	Ready:
		UBSP N 2 { A_UBShow(13); A_UBOn(); }
		UBSP O 2 A_UBShow(14);
		UBSP P 2 A_UBShow(15);
		UBSP Q 2 A_UBShow(16);
	ReadyLoop:
		UBSP AAA 1 A_UBReady(0);
		UBSP BBB 1 A_UBReady(1);
		UBSP CCC 1 A_UBReady(2);
		Loop;
	// FIRE: hold to lock on, throw with your arm (the swing itself is the attack -- see DoEffect)
	Fire:
		UBSP A 0 { A_UBShow(0); return A_UBHoldBegin(); }
	FireHold:
		UBSP A 1 { A_UBShow(0); return A_UBHold(); }
		Loop;
	// ALT: the Force push (ubqs_alt 1), or the second blade (ubqs_alt 0)
	AltFire:
		UBSP A 0 { A_UBShow(0); return A_UBAltFire(); }
	AltDone:
		UBSP A 8 A_UBShow(0);
		Goto ReadyLoop;
	// NEVER ENTERED. The engine registers a sprite name only when some state uses it, and MODELDEF stops
	// the game on a name it does not know -- so every size x colour x blades name the psprite is switched
	// to, and the thrown saber's, is named here once.
	GlowHold:
		G3BS A -1 Bright;
		Stop;

		UXFL H 0; UXFL I 0; UXFL J 0; UXFL K 0; UXFL L 0; UXFL M 0;
		G1BD A 0; G1BS A 0; G1CD A 0; G1CS A 0; G1GD A 0; G1GS A 0; G1OD A 0; G1OS A 0; G1PD A 0; G1PS A 0;

		G2GD A 0; G2GS A 0; G2OD A 0; G2OS A 0; G2PD A 0; G2PS A 0; G2RD A 0; G2RS A 0; G2WD A 0; G2WS A 0;

class UBQS_Saber : UBQS_SaberBase {}
class UBQS_SaberOff : UBQS_SaberBase
{
	Default
	{
		+WEAPON.OFFHANDWEAPON
		Weapon.SelectionOrder 2101;
	}
}

// ---- THE CLASH FLASH: a white-hot starburst where two blades meet -----------------------------------------
// One additive, fullbright billboard that blooms and fades in a fifth of a second. No light of its own (the
// saber's flash light does that), so it costs a sprite.
// A RUMBLE OF OUR OWN, WITH A LENGTH AND A STRENGTH. See UBQS_SaberBase.Rumble for why this exists
// and why it follows the pawn rather than sitting where it was spawned.
// ---- THE SWING, HEARD FROM THE BLADE ------------------------------------------------------
//
// A sound played on the player is a sound at the player's feet: in a headset the whoosh of a
// metre-long blade arrived from inside your chest, in the middle of your head, the same whatever
// you did with your arm. The engine spatialises a sound at the ACTOR that plays it, so the swing
// is played from here instead -- a silent emitter sitting on the blade's tip, following it every
// tic for as long as the sound lasts. The whoosh then comes from where the blade actually is, and
// sweeps across your head as the blade does.
//
// AND IT BENDS. Each tic this measures how fast the tip is closing on your head along the line
// between them -- the radial component, which is the only part of a velocity that shifts a pitch --
// and rides A_SoundPitch with it: rising while the blade comes at you, falling as it leaves. That
// is the whole of the Doppler effect, and on a blade swung at arm's length it is a real interval,
// not a subtlety: a 10 m/s pass is about a semitone each way.
//
// Sound only. Nothing here touches the playsim, and the emitter is spawned on every machine from
// the same swing decision the cut already is.
// ---- THE HUM, WHICH BELONGS TO THE BLADE --------------------------------------------------
//
// The idle hum was played on the player, which puts it at the player's feet and leaves the sound
// of a lit lightsaber coming out of the middle of your head. It lives here instead: a silent
// emitter at the blade's midpoint, carried with it every tic, holding the looping hum for as long
// as the blade is lit. Move the blade past your ear and the hum moves with it, and in a headset
// that is most of the difference between a lightsaber and a sound effect.
//
// It takes the same Doppler ride the swing does, at half strength -- a hum on a blade you are
// swinging really does bend, and it is the part you hear continuously rather than in bursts.
// ---- A CONTACT, HEARD WHERE IT HAPPENED ---------------------------------------------------
//
// The hum and the swing moved onto the blade; every other saber sound was still played on the
// player, which is the one place none of them happen. A clash is at the crossing point, a cut is
// at the body, a scorch is on the wall. All three are a position this code has already worked out
// to put its sparks at -- it was throwing the position away and playing the sound at your feet.
//
// So: a silent one-shot that sits where it happened for long enough to be heard out, then goes.
// Sound only, and spawned from a decision every machine already makes.
class UBQS_Ping : Actor
{
	int life;
	Default
	{
		+NOINTERACTION +NOBLOCKMAP +NOSECTOR +NOGRAVITY +DONTSPLASH +NOTONAUTOMAP +NOTIMEFREEZE
		RenderStyle "None";
	}
	// at: where it happened. The emitter never moves -- a clash stays where the blades met even if
	// you walk away from it, which is what makes it read as a place rather than as a cue.
	// NOT Play(): `play` is a scope keyword in ZScript and a method of that name is a fatal
	// "Unexpected 'play'" at every call site.
	static void At(Actor from, Vector3 at, Sound s, double vol, double pitch = 1.0)
	{
		if (!from) return;
		let cv = CVar.FindCVar('ubqs_swing_spatial');
		if (cv && cv.GetInt() == 0) { from.A_StartSound(s, CHAN_AUTO, 0, vol, ATTN_NORM, pitch); return; }
		let p = UBQS_Ping(Actor.Spawn('UBQS_Ping', at));
		if (!p) { from.A_StartSound(s, CHAN_AUTO, 0, vol, ATTN_NORM, pitch); return; }
		p.life = 70;		// two seconds: longer than any of these samples, and the tic loop ends it
		p.A_StartSound(s, CHAN_BODY, 0, vol, ATTN_NORM, pitch);
	}
	override void Tick()
	{
		Super.Tick();
		if (--life <= 0) Destroy();
	}
	States { Spawn: TNT1 A 1; Wait; }
}

class UBQS_Hummer : Actor
{
	Actor ear;
	Vector3 at;			// the blade's midpoint, written by the saber every tic
	double base;		// the pitch the saber wants from the swing speed, before the shift
	double lastR;
	Default
	{
		+NOINTERACTION +NOBLOCKMAP +NOSECTOR +NOGRAVITY +DONTSPLASH +NOTONAUTOMAP +NOTIMEFREEZE
		RenderStyle "None";
	}
	override void Tick()
	{
		Super.Tick();
		if (!ear) { A_StopSound(CHAN_BODY); Destroy(); return; }
		SetOrigin(at, true);
		let p = ear.player;
		Vector3 head = (ear.pos.xy, p ? p.viewz : ear.pos.z + ear.height * 0.8);
		double r = (at - head).Length();
		if (lastR > 0 && base > 0)
		{
			let cv = CVar.FindCVar('ubqs_doppler');
			double k = cv ? clamp(cv.GetFloat(), 0.0, 2.0) : 1.0;
			double shift = clamp((lastR - r) * 0.008 * k, -0.2, 0.2);
			A_SoundPitch(CHAN_BODY, clamp(base + shift, 0.5, 2.0));
		}
		lastR = r;
	}
	States { Spawn: TNT1 A 1; Wait; }
}

class UBQS_Swish : Actor
{
	Actor ear;			// whose head we are passing
	Vector3 tip;		// where the blade's tip is this tic, set by the saber
	double base;		// the pitch the swing started at, before any shift
	double lastR;		// the distance to the ear last tic
	int life;
	Default
	{
		+NOINTERACTION +NOBLOCKMAP +NOSECTOR +NOGRAVITY +DONTSPLASH +NOTONAUTOMAP +NOTIMEFREEZE
		RenderStyle "None";
	}
	override void Tick()
	{
		Super.Tick();
		if (!ear || life <= 0) { A_StopSound(CHAN_BODY); Destroy(); return; }
		life--;
		SetOrigin(tip, true);
		let p = ear.player;
		Vector3 head = (ear.pos.xy, p ? p.viewz : ear.pos.z + ear.height * 0.8);
		double r = (tip - head).Length();
		if (lastR > 0)
		{
			// closing speed in units per tic; positive while it comes at you. The engine's own sound
			// speed is irrelevant here -- this is a feel number, scaled by ubqs_doppler.
			double closing = (lastR - r);
			let cv = CVar.FindCVar('ubqs_doppler');
			double k = cv ? clamp(cv.GetFloat(), 0.0, 2.0) : 1.0;
			double shift = clamp(closing * 0.016 * k, -0.35, 0.35);
			A_SoundPitch(CHAN_BODY, clamp(base + shift, 0.5, 2.0));
		}
		lastR = r;
	}
	States { Spawn: TNT1 A 1; Wait; }
}

class UBQS_Buzzer : Actor
{
	Actor feels;
	Default { +NOINTERACTION +NOBLOCKMAP +NOSECTOR +NOGRAVITY +DONTSPLASH +NOTONAUTOMAP RenderStyle "None"; }
	override void Tick()
	{
		Super.Tick();
		if (!feels) { Destroy(); return; }
		SetOrigin(feels.pos, true);
	}
	States { Spawn: TNT1 A 20; Stop; }
}

class UBQS_HapticPuff : Actor
{
	Default { +NOINTERACTION +NOBLOCKMAP +BLOODLESSIMPACT +PAINLESS +NODAMAGETHRUST -ALWAYSPUFF RenderStyle "None"; }
	States { Spawn: TNT1 A 1; Stop; }
}

// ---- ONE COMBATFX EFFECT: a sprite (the owner's CombatFX set) played through its frames, growing and fading,
// gone when done. Additive; shade >= 0 draws a grey mask in that colour (AddShaded). No engine particles.
class UBQS_FX : Actor
{
	int life, total, tpf, nfr;
	double a0, grow;
	bool rev;
	Vector3 dv;        // per-tic drift, applied in Tick (the class is +NOINTERACTION: vel is never read)
	Default
	{
		RenderStyle "Add";
		Radius 1;
		Height 1;
		+NOINTERACTION
		+NOBLOCKMAP
		+BRIGHT
		+NOGRAVITY
		+NOTONAUTOMAP
		+FORCEXYBILLBOARD
		+DONTSPLASH
		+NOTELEPORT
		+ROLLSPRITE
		+ROLLCENTER
	}
	// `dv` drifts it, because this class's Tick never applied vel and smoke that sits still is not smoke.
	// `soft` drops it off the additive/BRIGHT default, because additive smoke is only more glow. Both
	// default to exactly today, so every existing caller is unchanged.
	static UBQS_FX Fx(Vector3 at, Name spr, int nfr, int tpf, double sc, double a = 1.0, int shade = -1, double grow = 1.0, bool rev = false, Vector3 dv = (0, 0, 0), bool soft = false)
	{
		let f = UBQS_FX(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_FX", at));
		if (!f) return null;
		f.sprite = GetSpriteIndex(spr);
		f.nfr = max(nfr, 1);
		f.tpf = max(tpf, 1);
		f.total = f.nfr * f.tpf;
		f.life = f.total;
		f.rev = rev;
		f.frame = rev ? f.nfr - 1 : 0;
		f.scale = (sc, sc);
		f.a0 = a;
		f.alpha = a;
		f.grow = grow;
		f.roll = frandom[UBQSFx](0, 360);
		f.dv = dv;
		if (soft)
		{
			// smoke, not light: off Add, off BRIGHT, lit by the room like any other sprite
			f.A_SetRenderStyle(a, STYLE_Translucent);
			f.bBright = false;
		}
		else if (shade >= 0)
		{
			f.A_SetRenderStyle(a, STYLE_AddShaded);
			f.SetShade(shade);
		}
		return f;
	}
	override void Tick()
	{
		if (isFrozen()) return;
		if (--life < 0) { Destroy(); return; }
		int k = clamp((total - life - 1) / tpf, 0, nfr - 1);
		frame = rev ? nfr - 1 - k : k;
		if (grow != 1.0) scale *= grow;
		if (dv != (0, 0, 0)) SetOrigin(level.Vec3Offset(pos, dv), true);
		double t = life / double(total);
		alpha = (nfr == 1) ? a0 * t : a0 * min(1.0, t * 2.5);
	}
	States
	{
	Spawn:
		UXSP A -1 Bright;
		Stop;
	Register:
		UXPD A 0;
		UXST A 0;
		UXLT A 0;
		UXHF A 0;
		UXRG A 0;
		UXPL A 0;
		UXGL A 0;
		UXEM A 0;
		UXRE A 0;
		Stop;
	}
}

// ---- THE BEAM'S GLOW: nested closed additive capsules round the blade (ubqs.py / volglow.py -- volumetric
// from any angle, no plane edges). Model +Z is the beam, z 0 the emitter: turned by the actor's angle and pitch
// (models.cpp: +Z goes to (sin p cos a, sin p sin a, cos p)), so pitch = acos(dir.z), angle = the beam's
// heading. Scale.Y (model Z) stretches it to the beam's length (built 26 long), Scale.X sets its radius.
class UBQS_BeamGlow : Actor
{
	Default
	{
		RenderStyle "Add";
		Alpha 0.6;
		Radius 1;
		Height 1;
		+NOINTERACTION
		+NOBLOCKMAP
		+NOGRAVITY
		+NOTONAUTOMAP
		+DONTSPLASH
		+NOTELEPORT
		+BRIGHT
		+INTERPOLATEANGLES
	}
	// PLACED BY THE SABER, in its DoEffect (the player ticks before this actor; the engine has already set
	// Prev = Pos and PrevAngles = Angles for this tic). The renderer then slides Prev -> here, angles too
	// (+INTERPOLATEANGLES). The saber hands us a PREDICTED pose (UBQS_SaberBase.GlowPredict), so that slide
	// lands on the live blade. jump: no history to slide from -- clear the interpolation (no ghost sweep).
	// core: the white-hot inner shells (UBC*), else the coloured halo (UBH*) -- vgsplit.py
	// snapA / snapL: no slide this tic for the turn / for the base (a stop, a reversal, or coming to rest)
	static UBQS_BeamGlow Put(UBQS_BeamGlow g, bool core, Vector3 from, Vector3 dir, double length, double w, int col, int q, double a, bool jump, bool snapA = false, bool snapL = false)
	{
		if (!g)
		{
			g = UBQS_BeamGlow(Actor.Spawn("UBQS_BeamGlow", from));
			if (!g) return null;
			jump = true;
		}
		g.Place(core, from, dir, length, w, col, q, a, jump, snapA, snapL);
		return g;
	}
	// (telemetry, ubqs_diag 2) the angles the engine lerps FROM this tic -- PrevAngles is not in ZScript
	double pYaw, pPitch, pRoll;
	Vector3 faceDir;          // the last facing direction (kept when the eye is on the beam's line)
	void Place(bool core, Vector3 from, Vector3 dir, double length, double w, int col, int q, double a, bool jump, bool snapA = false, bool snapL = false)
	{
		// low / med / high / ultra
		static const String SPRC[] = { "UBC1", "UBC2", "UBC3", "UBC4" };
		static const String SPRH[] = { "UBH1", "UBH2", "UBH3", "UBH4" };
		// Prev is where the glow was drawn at the end of last tic -- the engine set it so this tic; said
		// again here so the slide always starts from the last placed pose
		Prev = pos;
		Vector3 oldPos = pos;
		pYaw = angle;
		pPitch = pitch;
		pRoll = roll;
		SetOrigin(from, true);
		// THE FACING (build 51, vgface.py): the shells are rolled about the beam so their +Y meridian faces the
		// viewer's eye -- the part of (eye - beam) square to the beam, the same all along it -- so each shell's
		// texture fades smoothly to nothing at its own silhouette (no rings). The model's axes: +X = F x D, +Y =
		// F, +Z = D give angle / pitch from +X (an actor's forward) and roll = atan2(F.z, D.z) (proto/xf.py).
		Vector3 F = UBQS_Data.EyeOf(players[consoleplayer]) - from;
		F -= dir * (F dot dir);
		double fl = F.Length();
		if (fl > 0.05) faceDir = F / fl;
		F = faceDir - dir * (faceDir dot dir);
		if (F.Length() < 0.01) F = (abs(dir.z) < 0.9) ? (0, 0, 1) - dir * dir.z : (1, 0, 0) - dir * dir.x;
		F = F.Unit();
		faceDir = F;
		Vector3 X = F cross dir;
		double yaw = VectorAngle(X.x, X.y);
		double pit = -asin(clamp(X.z, -1.0, 1.0));
		double rol = atan2(F.z, dir.z);
		// (yaw + 180, -180 - pitch, roll + 180) is the same pose: take whichever is nearer the last, so the
		// engine's per-axis angle lerp (deltaangle: wrap-safe) never swings the long way round
		double c0 = abs(DeltaAngle(angle, yaw)) + abs(DeltaAngle(pitch, pit)) + abs(DeltaAngle(roll, rol));
		double c1 = abs(DeltaAngle(angle, yaw + 180.0)) + abs(DeltaAngle(pitch, -180.0 - pit)) + abs(DeltaAngle(roll, rol + 180.0));
		if (c1 < c0) { yaw += 180.0; pit = -180.0 - pit; rol += 180.0; }
		angle = Normalize180(yaw);
		pitch = Normalize180(pit);
		roll = Normalize180(rol);
		// the capsule is built for a 26-unit blade, z 0 at the emitter. NO pixelstretch factor any more: the
		// glow's MODELDEF blocks now declare CorrectPixelStretch, which moves the engine's 1/pixelstretch
		// squash out of MODEL space (models.cpp:198-202, innermost, so it rotates with the beam) into WORLD
		// space (models.cpp:157-161) -- which is where the hand matrix always put it
		// (hw_openxrdevice.cpp:448, ahead of the controller rotations) and therefore where the SABER'S HILT
		// now has it too. The old `* level.pixelstretch` cancelled the model-space squash exactly, so the beam
		// was right in map units at every angle but 20% too LONG on screen when vertical; with the flag there
		// is nothing left to cancel and keeping the factor would be a straight 20% overshoot.
		// THIS LINE AND THE 64 CorrectPixelStretch KEYWORDS SHIP TOGETHER. Either one alone trades today's
		// detachment for a hilt-to-beam LENGTH mismatch at exactly the overhead-chop angles.
		scale = (w, max(length, 0.5) / 26.0);
		int qi = clamp(q, 1, 4) - 1;
		sprite = GetSpriteIndex(core ? SPRC[qi] : SPRH[qi]);
		frame = col;
		alpha = a;
		if (jump || snapA)
		{
			// the angles can only be cleared with the position: clear both, then give the base its slide back
			// unless it stops too
			ClearInterpolation();
			if (!jump && !snapL) Prev = oldPos;
			pYaw = angle;
			pPitch = pitch;
			pRoll = roll;
		}
		else if (snapL) Prev = pos;
		if (jump) { pYaw = angle; pPitch = pitch; pRoll = roll; }
	}
	States
	{
	Spawn:
		UBH3 A -1 Bright;
		Stop;
	Register:
		UBC1 A 0;
		UBC2 A 0;
		UBC3 A 0;
		UBC4 A 0;
		UBH1 A 0;
		UBH2 A 0;
		UBH4 A 0;
		Stop;
	}
}

// ---- THE SABER ITSELF, IN THE WORLD -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE OWNER, 10-01: "the blade detaches from the hilt when i swing". It had to. The hilt was a psprite, and
// RenderHUDModel re-poses a psprite model from the LIVE controller every frame, per eye, at zero latency
// (models.cpp:226 -> VRMode::GetWeaponTransform -> hw_openxrdevice.cpp:431-459). The beam was UBQS_BeamGlow, a
// world actor moved once per 35 Hz tic and interpolated between. Two layers drawn at two different moments
// cannot agree, and no overlap slider was ever going to make them. So the hilt is a world actor too, placed in
// the SAME tic from the SAME predicted pose as its beam (UBQS_SaberBase.PoseTick). One rigid saber: they
// cannot disagree any more.
//
// WHY THIS IS A SECOND ACTOR AND NOT ONE ACTOR WITH THE BEAM. RenderStyle is per ACTOR and it picks the whole
// draw pass: a translucent or additive model goes to GLDL_TRANSLUCENT, drawn later with depth writes OFF and
// depth-sorted; an opaque one goes to GLDL_MODELS (hw_drawlistadd.cpp:141-152). An opaque hilt and an additive
// beam physically cannot be the same actor. They are instead placed from ONE set of expressions in ONE tic,
// which is what "they cannot disagree" actually requires.
//
// THE TRANSFORM, solved against BOTH matrix chains rather than copied from the HUD block -- copying cannot
// work, because the HUD path adds a 0.01 pre-scale, a translate(0, 5, 30), vr_3dweaponOffset*, a
// rotate(90, Y) and vr_weaponScale, none of which exist in RenderModel, and it pitches about X and rolls
// about Z where the world path pitches about Z and rolls about X:
//     angle = HA()  == (off ? OffhandAngle : AttackAngle) + 90      -- the SAME formula for both hands
//     pitch = HP()  == -(off ? OffhandPitch : AttackPitch)          -- the SAME for both hands
//     roll  = HR()  == +(off ? OffhandRoll  : AttackRoll)           -- the SAME, and NOT negated
//     MODELDEF: UseActorPitch + UseActorRoll + CorrectPixelStretch, no Offset at all, and
//               Scale 1 1 1 on the hand the engine does NOT reflect / Scale 1 -1 1 on the hand it does
//     Scale    = UBQS_Data.WorldScale(sizeIdx)
//     position = the predicted hand + UBQS_Data.WorldNudge(...)
// Built as 4x4 matrices from the engine's own source and compared pose by pose, the two chains agree to
// 1e-15 -- in the rotation AND in the origin, on both hands, at every angle, with vr_3dweaponOffset set and
// with the saber part-raised. This is not a fitted guess.
//
// A FREE WIN THAT FALLS OUT OF THE MOVE: the psprite hilt was OCCLUDING its own glow. HUD models write depth
// into a hacked range of [0, 0.3] (hw_models.cpp:91-97, "hack the depth range to prevent view model from
// poking into walls"), nearer than the entire world, and the additive glow is drawn later in the translucent
// pass with the depth TEST still on -- so the halo was depth-rejected everywhere the hilt's silhouette covered
// it. Both are ordinary world geometry now, depth-sorted against each other properly.
// DO NOT read that as "the dim band at the emitter is fixed". It is not: the beam's base is still pushed
// ubqs_glow_overlap_core / _halo units BELOW the emitter mouth, i.e. INSIDE a hilt of 0.62 radius, and an
// opaque hilt writing depth first can hide MORE of that fade-in tail than the flat near-range hack did, not
// less. Look at the joint standing dead still before deciding, and sweep the two overlap sliders there.
//
// WHAT THE MOVE COSTS, so nobody is surprised in the headset.
//  * THE HILT IS NO LONGER LIVE. The psprite was re-posed every frame; this is a pose sampled between one and
//    two tics ago (P_Ticker snapshots Prev/PrevAngles for EVERY actor before any thinker runs,
//    p_tick.cpp:151-163), which GlowPredict then leads forward. The saber stops detaching from itself and
//    starts swimming as a whole. An opaque hilt also has no ubqs_glow_motionfade to hide the residual the way
//    the beam's translucent core does. ubqs_diag 2 now prints that residual as "hilt vs real hand", in map
//    units, measured at the hand -- read THAT line, not the beam's "base" figure, which is offset by
//    ubqs_glow_overlap_halo and measured a lever-arm up the blade.
//  * IT CAN BE CUT BY WALLS. BeginDrawHUDModel sets SetDepthClamp(true) and compresses the psprite's depth
//    into the near 30% precisely so the view model cannot poke into walls (hw_models.cpp:88-97);
//    BeginDrawModel does neither. Push your hand through a wall or a door frame in a corridor and the hilt
//    will be sliced at the surface. There is no mod-side answer to this; it is the trade, and
//    ubqs_world_saber 0 is the way out.
//  * IT IS LIT BY THE WORLD, deliberately (no +BRIGHT). It will sit inside the blade's own UBQS_Light and be
//    washed in blade colour, and it takes the sector's light level instead of the psprite lighting path -- so
//    in a dark map it may read darker than he is used to. If it reads flat, fake or wrongly tinted, +BRIGHT on
//    this actor is the one-word answer and ubqs_lights 0 isolates whether the blade light is the cause.
class UBQS_WorldSaber : Actor
{
	Default
	{
		Radius 1;
		Height 1;
		+NOINTERACTION
		+NOBLOCKMAP
		+NOGRAVITY
		+NOTONAUTOMAP
		+DONTSPLASH
		+NOTELEPORT
		// WITHOUT THIS THE HILT'S ORIENTATION STEPS AT 35 Hz WHILE ITS POSITION GLIDES: a world model's
		// position is interpolated by default, but its ANGLES only with this flag, and the same interpolated
		// DRotator then feeds the yaw, the UseActorPitch pitch and the UseActorRoll roll (models.cpp:92-95,
		// actor.h:1502-1513). This is the single most important flag on the actor.
		+INTERPOLATEANGLES
	}
	// DELIBERATELY NOT SET:
	//   +NOSECTOR -- an actor is only drawn if the BSP walk reaches a sector it touches
	//     (hw_bsp.cpp:602-626, sec->touching_renderthings); NOSECTOR makes it permanently invisible.
	//   +BRIGHT -- the hilt is metal, and being lit by the world is half the gain of being in the world. See
	//     the note above; UBQS_BeamGlow sets +BRIGHT because it IS the light, and this is not.
	//   +FLOATBOB, SpriteRotation, WorldOffset -- SpriteRotation (models.cpp:150) and WorldOffset
	//     (hw_sprites.cpp:936-938) are read RAW with no interpolation, so either would put the 35 Hz staircase
	//     straight back into a saber we went to this trouble to smooth; FLOATBOB *is* interpolated
	//     (AActor::GetBobOffset takes ticfrac, actorinlines.h) but a hilt in your hand must not bob at all.
	// NOT +NOBLOCKMAP's job but worth saying: every actor search in this mod is a BlockThingsIterator or a
	// ThinkerIterator on a named class, so +NOBLOCKMAP keeps this out of all of them -- the hilt can never be
	// cut, clashed with or deflected off.

	// (telemetry parity with UBQS_BeamGlow, ubqs_diag 2) the angles the engine lerps FROM this tic.
	// PrevAngles is not exposed to ZScript at all, so this shadow copy is the only way to know what the
	// renderer is actually drawing at a given TicFrac.
	double pYaw, pPitch, pRoll;

	// PLACED BY THE SABER, from its DoEffect -- exactly as UBQS_BeamGlow.Place is, and for exactly the same
	// reason: P_Ticker has already done ClearInterpolation on EVERY actor for this tic (Prev = Pos,
	// PrevAngles = Angles, p_tick.cpp:151-163) BEFORE the player thinks, so anything written here is
